title: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting and phenotypic characterization of human fibro-adipogenic progenitors
protocol: Place the muscle tissue sample in a petri dish.
Keep the muscle tissue moist by adding 2–3 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media if needed.
Mince the muscle tissue using sterile surgical scissors to obtain a slurry substance.
Remove all visible connective tissue and fat from the tissue using sterile forceps and scissors.
Mince the tissue well to increase surface area for enzyme digestion.
Weigh the minced muscle tissue if cell yield per mg of tissue is relevant.
Transfer the minced muscle tissue to a C-tube.
Place the C-tube on the gentleMACS dissociator.
Add heaters to maintain temperature during digestion.
Choose a muscle digestion program, such as 37_mr_SMDK1 (1 hour and 1 minute).
Pause the process at 61 minutes to check for any clogging of rotating blades.
Add 8 mL of 4°C HAMS F10+ wash media to each C-tube to stop the enzymatic digestion.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer on a 50 mL falcon tube.
Wash the filter using 2 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media to remove surface tension.
Aspirate the digested muscle suspension in and out of a 20 mL syringe using an 18 G needle.
Eject the suspension to the wall of the tube to be gentle on cells and avoid foaming.
Repeat five times to ensure single cell suspension.
Remove all of the muscle suspension from the syringe by aspiration.
Aspirate the entire suspension into the syringe and remove the needle.
Eject the suspension onto the 70 μm cell strainer on a 50 mL falcon tube to remove debris by gravity.
Wash the empty C-tube(s) twice using 5–10 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media.
Transfer the wash media to the 70 μm cell strainer(s).
Collect any remaining liquid hanging underneath the cell strainer by pipetting.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Add 1 mL of StemMACS cryopreservation buffer to the pellet(s).
Resuspend the cells gently by pipetting up and down 2–4 times using a 1,000 μL pipette or larger.
Transfer the solution to cryotube(s) using a pipette.
Place the cryotube(s) in a freezing container.
Store at −80°C until further use.
Move cells from the freezing container to storage boxes after freezing has occurred (∼ 12–24 h).
Recommend moving cells to a −150°C freezer after 24 hours for preservation if available.
If -150°C freezer is not available, store cells at −80°C.
Sort the cells within 2–4 weeks after freezing for highest viability and best cell performance.
Incubate the sample(s) to be sorted using FACS with antibodies.
Prepare FMO controls alongside or at the pause point during antibody incubation of samples for sorting.
Prepare compensation samples at the pause point of antibody incubation for sorting samples.
Analyze FMO controls, compensation samples, and unstained control on the cell sorter before running full samples.
Add 10 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media (stored at 4°C) to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Prepare one 15 mL falcon tube per sample being sorted.
Thaw the digested muscle sample(s) quickly in a 37°C water bath until only a small amount of ice is left in the tube.
Wipe down the tube(s) using 70% ethanol and place it at the sterile tissue culture hood.
Transfer the thawed or fresh sample(s) to 15 mL falcon tube(s) containing 10 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media.
Wash the original tube(s) with 1 mL of HAMS F10+ wash media, then transfer the wash media to the 15 mL falcon tube(s).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Add 200–400 μL of HAMS F10+ wash media to the 15 mL falcon tube(s) to reach a final volume of approximately 500 μL.
Resuspend the pellet by gently pipetting up and down 2–4 times.
Transfer 50 μL of sample from each 15 mL falcon tube to individual 2 mL Eppendorf tubes using a pipette.
Place the Eppendorf tubes on ice and add additional 150 μL of HAMS F10+ wash media to each Eppendorf tube.
Save the tubes on ice for later use as unstained control samples.
Transfer 20 μL of sample from each 15 mL falcon tube to individual 2 mL Eppendorf tubes using a pipette.
Place the Eppendorf tubes on ice and add additional 100 μL HAMS F10+ wash media to each tube.
Save the tubes on ice for later use as compensation samples (propidium iodide).
Transfer 20 μL of sample from each 15 mL falcon tube to 5 individual 2 mL Eppendorf tubes using a pipette.
Place the Eppendorf tubes on ice and add additional 100 μL HAMS F10+ wash media to each.
Save the tubes on ice for later use as fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) controls.
Place the sample(s) on a rotator or tilting table at 4°C in the dark for 30–40 min.
Wrap the tube(s) in tinfoil to prevent light from reaching the samples.
Add 10 ml of HAMS F10+ wash media to the 15 ml falcon tube(s).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Add 500 μl of HAMS F10+ wash media to the 15 ml falcon tube(s) for small biopsies or up to 2 ml for larger biopsies.
Resuspend the cell pellet by pipetting up and down 2–4 times.
Place a 30 μm cell strainer on a 5 ml FACS tube.
Transfer the solution(s) to the cell strainer(s) by using a pipette.
Remove debris and aggregates by gravity filtration.
Filter the non-stained control prepared in step 32.
Collect any remaining liquid hanging underneath the cell strainer(s) using a pipette.
Wash the 15 mL falcon tube(s) twice with 500 μL of HAMS F10+ wash media.
Transfer the 2 × 500 μL of HAMS F10+ wash media to the cell strainer.
Prepare collection tubes for the FACS by adding 500 μL or 100 μL of HAMS F10+ wash media as appropriate.
Mark the tubes with ID and cell type.
Place the tubes on ice.
Add Propidium iodide to the cells immediately before sorting to distinguish viable from non-viable cells.
Perform all procedures in a ventilated sterile tissue culture hood.
Take 120 μl samples for FMO controls.
Add antibodies to Eppendorf tubes according to Table 2 recommendations.
Place Eppendorf tubes on a rotator or tilting table at 4°C in the dark for 30-40 minutes.
Wrap tubes in tinfoil to prevent light from reaching the samples.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Add 250 μl of HAMS F10+ wash media to Eppendorf tubes.
Resuspend cell pellets by pipetting up and down 2–4 times.
Add Propidium iodide to the cells immediately before sorting to distinguish viable from non-viable cells (do not add PI to the PI FMO sample).
Heat an Eppendorf tube containing 120 μL of unstained sample at 60°C–70°C for 1 minute.
Place the heated tube on ice immediately after heating.
Add 10 μL Propidium iodide immediately before sorting.
Mark the tube as PI control.
Add one drop of UltraComp eBeads to each of five Eppendorf tubes.
Add one antibody (two for FITC-conjugated CD45 and CD31 antibodies) to each tube.
Add one antibody to each Eppendorf tube containing UltraComp eBeads.
Vortex the samples and incubate for 15 min at ∼22°C in dark.
Add 1 mL of PBS to each Eppendorf tube to wash away residual antibody.
Centrifuge at 800 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 300 μL of PBS to each tube to wash the side of the tube where the pellet is located.
Pipette up and down 2–4 times to resuspend the pellet.
Vortex.
Wrap the tubes in tinfoil to prevent light from reaching the samples.
Set up the cell sorter with a 100 μm nozzle and 20 psi.
Allow the system to stabilize.
Run CS&T beads to quality control the instrument.
Adjust the stream by changing the amplitude and frequency.
Ensure uniform drops are forming.
Adjust the drop delay until 97%–100% deflection of Accudrop beads is achieved.
Apply a suitable voltage to adjust side streams for droplets to fall into collection tubes.
Adjust electrical charge on side streams to ensure droplets fall into the middle of the collection tubes.
Set up an experiment using the software.
Use “purity” as the precision sort mask in the sort layout.
Run non-stained sample (prepared in step 32) for setting PMT voltages.
Save at least 10 μL of the non-stained sample for later use.
Run a 5–10 μL full stained sample (prepared in steps 21–54).
Ensure no fluorochromes are off scale.
Initiate compensation setup in FACS software.
Run single colored beads for FACS compensation sample (prepared in steps 65–73).
Run propidium iodide compensation sample (prepared in steps 61–64) following designated software steps.
On the FSC-A and SCC plot create a gate to collect the cells of the right size and to exclude debris.
On the FSC-A and FSC-H plot create a gate to collect single cells only.
Create gates to collect skeletal muscle stem cells (MuSCs) (CD34-CD56+CD82+CD45-CD31-).
Create gates to collect fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) (CD34+CD56-CD45-CD31-).
Add 10 μL of PI to the sample being sorted immediately before sorting.
Run the sample according to the expected percentage of each cell population as indicated in Table 4.
Adjust the gates for cell populations to be centered within the gates based on Table 4 guidelines.
Sort cells at a flow rate of 3–6, aiming for 2,000–5,000 events per second and never exceeding 8,000 events per second.
Gently vortex the sorted sample(s) after sorting is complete.
Freeze the cells if they are to be used later for RNA isolation.
Transfer the solution(s) containing the sorted cells to RNAse free Eppendorf tubes.
Mark the Eppendorf tubes with ID and cell type.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Place all the Eppendorf tubes facing the same direction with the opening of the lid upwards.
Add a gel loading tip on top of the pipetting tip to avoid hitting the pellet area.
Store the tube(s) at −80°C until analysis.
Snap freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen before storage if necessary.
Plate the cells at a density of approximately 1 × 10^4/cm^2 for cell culture experiments.
Add growth media at an appropriate amount for the well size chosen.
Place the cell culture tray(s) in a 37°C 5% CO2 incubator.
Change the media every other day for cells.
Warm media or PBS in a 37°C water bath before adding it to the cell culture.
Eject media to the wall of the well when changing media to avoid disturbing the interception of the cells.
Store unused media at 4°C for up to one month.
Plate cells at a density of approximately 1 × 10^4/cm^2 for proliferation detection.
Add HAMS F10+ wash media in an appropriate amount based on the well size.
Add EdU from the Click-iTTM EdU cell proliferation kit in HAMS F10+ wash media at concentration of 10 μM upon plating of the cells.
Store the media at 4°C for up to one month when it is not being used.
Aspirate the media after incubation period (24–48 h for MuSCs, 48–72 h for FAPs).
Fix the cells using 4% paraformaldehyde for 5 min.
Wash the cells ×3 using 1× PBS.
Allow the cells to grow to approximately 95% confluence before differentiation.
Wash the cells once using warm sterile 1×PBS.
Add myogenic differentiation media in an appropriate volume for the well size chosen.
Replace the media with fresh media every 2 days.
Observe cell differentiation using a light microscope on a regular basis.
Fix cells using 4% paraformaldehyde for 5 min once fully differentiated.
Wash the cells ×3 using 1×PBS.
Allow the cells to grow to approximately 70% for fibrogenic differentiation and 95% confluence for adipogenic differentiation.
Wash the cells once using warm sterile 1×PBS.
Add proper differentiation media for either fibrogenic or adipogenic differentiation of FAPs at a volume appropriate for the well size chosen.
Replace the media with fresh differentiation media every 2 days.
Store the media at 4°C when it is not being used.
Observe the cells on a regular basis using a light microscope.
Fix the cells using 4% paraformaldehyde for 5 min.
Wash the cells ×3 using PBS.
